thread:
maria (Customer): Hi, hitting intermittent 429s + high p95 after a traffic burst this morning. Customer app does many small chat requests (~1-4 tokens) concurrent. No recent code change on their side.

maria (Customer): Example: burst of ~800 reqs/s for ~30s, then a flood of 429s and latency spikes. We suspect KV cache or batching interactions.

emma (Support): Sorry you're blocked — we started digging. Can you paste a minimal repro (curl + headers) and the tenant id? Also any request IDs you saw.

maria (Customer): Tenant: org-8675309. Sample curl: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"rwd-3b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'`

maria (Customer): From client logs: `x-request-id: 8f9c2a` and `x-redwood-tenant: org-8675309`. We also captured a server-side 429 body: `{"error":"rate_limit","message":"request quota exceeded"}`

emma (Support): Thanks. I can see an alert for org-8675309 around 2026-03-10T14:02Z: short-term quota exhaustion + elevated batch queue lengths. API bot shows backend returns 429 and increase in KV cache miss ratio.

api-bot: [system] Detected burst window: 2026-03-10T14:01:58 -> 2026-03-10T14:02:34, peak qps 820, avg batch latency rose from 12ms -> 110ms.

raj (SRE): Quick theory: small, highly concurrent requests cause many small batches -> batching window fills and KV cache sees prefix-starvation. If cache miss+prefetch paths kick in under pressure, it can look like "perceived throttling" because warmup and batch backpressure delay token servicing.

alex (Eng): Agreed. Two interacting effects we've seen: 1) continuous batching window increases latency when queue spikes; 2) KV cache evictions/prefix contention cause spikes in cache misses which amplify backend load.

emma (Support): Actionable repro steps for us: 1) Can you reproduce with a traffic generator that issues 1–3 token prompts at 800 qps for 30s? 2) Capture the X-Request-ID and the model variant. 3) Provide client inter-arrival histogram (p50/p95/p99).

maria (Customer): We'll run a loadtest tomorrow morning and drop logs here. Meanwhile, any mitigations we can try now? Customer is on a tight SLO.

raj (SRE): Short-term mitigations you can try immediately: reduce concurrency (client-side leaky bucket) or coalesce small prompts into multi-turn requests (where feasible). Also increase client-side retries with exponential backoff for 429s.

alex (Eng): On our side we can: 1) temporarily raise burst allowance for org-8675309 (manual quota bump) to see if 429s stop, 2) lower batching max window from 40ms -> 20ms for the backend pool serving that tenant to reduce queue delay (will slightly increase per-token cost), 3) enable a conservative KV-prefetch smoothing flag we have in staging to avoid mass-prefetch during sudden bursts.

emma (Support): I've queued an urgent config change request to try a manual burst bump + enable smoothing. If the customer agrees, we'll apply during your load test window.

maria (Customer): Please do the burst bump. Also can you explain the "perceived throttling" term so the customer understands root cause when we report back?

raj (SRE): Perceived throttling = requests are delayed by queueing/backpressure (batching + cache warmup) and look like throttling to the client (429s or long tail latency) even though raw capacity might exist for warmed-up hot keys. It's especially common with lots of tiny independent requests that can't be batched efficiently.

alex (Eng): Long-term fixes: 1) smarter prefix-aware KV eviction (avoid evicting hot conversational prefixes), 2) adaptive batching that shrinks window under tiny-payload regimes, 3) tenant-aware warm pools for customers that have bursty short prompts. We'll prioritize in next sprint if reproducible.

emma (Support): Next steps: - maria to run the loadtest and paste logs/ids here (we'll coordinate time) - I will initiate manual burst bump + enable smoothing flag during test - eng/sre to watch telemetry and revert if needed.

maria (Customer): Thanks all. Scheduling load test for 2026-03-11 09:00 UTC and will post results. 

emma (Support): Great, tagged as high-priority. Assigning to raj + alex to standby during the window. :thumbsup:

raj (SRE): Also, maria — if you can include a small sample of request payloads (esp. prefixes) we'll check for prefix-starvation patterns.

maria (Customer): Will share. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

emma (Support): Closing loop later with postmortem draft including mitigation + recommended client changes.
